notes: DISCOVERED during the nahb-hmi-2026-11-17 initial-research adjacency sweep (2026-09-06), from the publisher's own 2026 schedule. Why it earns its own row rather than a line in that ledger: it is the CONTROL for the one caution the November edition cannot clear. 2026-11-17 is a stacked morning (retail sales and import/export prices 08:30, industrial production 09:15, MTIS 10:00) and 2026-12-16 is stacked identically; this calendar currently tracks NOTHING on 2026-10-19, and the tracked October stack has cleared by then — CPI 10-14, retail sales and PPI 10-15, import/export prices and opex 10-16, FOMC blackout start 10-17. So this is, on the calendar as it stands, the corridor's one HMI morning with the 10:00 slot to itself. Stated as a limit rather than smoothed: the October 2026 G.17 date was NOT verified this session (federalreserve.gov/releases/g17/g17_release_dates.htm 404s as of 2026-09-06 and the g17.xml feed carries only elapsed releases), so whichever lane researches this id should confirm it before relying on the unstacked framing. The proposing lane measured that the split matters for exactly one metric: on the 34 HMI days that shared a morning with G.17, SPY's overnight gap ran 0.4828% against a 0.3275% clean baseline (p=0.0385), while the 44 unstacked HMI days ran 0.3391% (p=0.85) — dead baseline. So an unstacked HMI day is where the sentiment channel, if it existed, would be visible without a 09:15 print in front of it. It does not exist on the evidence to date (ITB open->close on the 78 HMI days 0.9559% vs 0.9627%, p=0.96; the paired sentiment-vs-data test over 71 consecutive-session pairs is 35/71 = 49.3%, sign test p=1.00), which makes 10-19 a cheap out-of-sample confirmation rather than a new hypothesis. Structural note carried forward: 10-19 is the trading day immediately before housing-starts-2026-10-20, the 91.0% D-1 pattern again, and that starts print is one of 2026's four SOLO GDPNow vintages per the housing-starts-2026-11-18 ledger — so the pair is the corridor's cleanest sentiment-then-data sequence of the year. Proposed as an estimate; nothing here licenses an entry.
